html:
SMTO-ART-0003 — A Gateway couldn't set up a temporary folder for a command

GUID: d4ce4ea3-6f94-44b6-8889-a55372079317
Slug: tmp-mapping-failed
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • Before running a command, the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) prepares private folders for the task. It couldn't set them up, so the command didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running the Gateway has free disk space and that its storage is connected and not read-only. The Gateway creates these folders on that computer and stops if it can't write them.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that Gateway. It confirms the Gateway is running and reachable before you try the command again.
  3. Then select Continue task if the task shows it, or send your request again as a new message. The command never started, so running it again won't do it twice.

What success looks like

  • The command runs on the Gateway and its output appears in the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway, mentioning whether its storage was moved or changed recently. Don't delete the Gateway's artifacts folder; it holds files from your tasks.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway refused to launch a shell or privileged command (executed=false, process_state failed_to_start) because TmpMappingError was raised while creating or validating the run's managed temp, artifact and scratch directories.

What this means

  • Shell/privileged execution catches TmpMappingError while constructing the managed temporary-workspace execution path. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Shell/privileged execution catches TmpMappingError while constructing the managed temporary-workspace execution path.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect run/conversation workspace mapping and the underlying mapping subtype before assuming package absence.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, check the Gateway log and the run workspace under the Gateway artifact root (GATEWAY_ARTIFACT_ROOT) for missing, unwritable or mismatched OF_RUN_TEMP_DIR, OF_RUN_ARTIFACT_DIR or OF_RUN_SCRATCH_DIR paths (artifact_wrong_scope), free space and permissions; on Linux with /tmp mapping, confirm bubblewrap and /proc/self/ns/user are available. The command was not started, so it can be rerun once the workspace validates.
  • Inspect the owning run, selected Gateway and supported temporary workspace state before publication.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended execution envelope uses a valid supported workspace mapping.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
